scenario.note: Only one of the hours 22-23, 07-08, or 11-12 may have stored energy; the rule enforces that the sum of stored energy in these hours is zero, meaning at most one hour has positive storage (and the others have zero).

The battery stored energy is allowed to be above zero in at most one of the hours 22-23, 07-08, and 11-12. This is modeled as a logical rule ensuring that at most one of the three hourly soc values exceeds zero.
The rule limits the number of hours in which the battery stored energy is above zero to at most one, among the specified hours.
The rule ensures that if the battery has stored energy above zero in hour 16-17, then at least 10 kW must be discharged in hour 21-22.

The rule enforces that the stored energy in hour 13-14 is either zero or at least 20 kWh. This is modeled as two mutually exclusive conditions: either soc is zero or soc is at least 20. However, since the model is linear, a logical rule is required to capture the 'either/or' condition. Thus, a logical rule is added to ensure that at least one of the two conditions holds: soc == 0 or soc >= 20.
The rule enforces that the stored energy in hour 13-14 is either zero or at least 20 kWh, modeled as a logical constraint via a relative rule with factor 0 and a minimum of 20.
